## What a counter cannot see

**Two readings, both from the document.** SABER (arXiv:2608.27963) branches the
prefix at every "Wait" into a neutral and an adversarial probe and stops when
the two agree; it is one of the few in this family to report probe overhead
(3.8% of tokens) and wall-clock latency (48.8% shorter) separately from token
counts, though it never says whether its own compression ratios are gross or
net of that overhead, and Table 1 cannot be reconciled with Table 3 from the
paper alone. The abduction paper (arXiv:2609.01867) is not a stopping method:
it correlates reasoning-token count with human reaction time per item and
finds every one of eight models significant, which gives this topic an
external criterion for how long a problem should take — neither accuracy nor
an estimated lower bound — and a caution, since humans score below chance on
the items the models get wrong.

**DEER's entry was rewritten because its standing changed, not its mechanism.**
The old text carried the method's self-report (19.1–80.1% of tokens cut,
accuracy up 0.3–5.0%). Independent runs do not reproduce the accuracy gain:
SABER puts DEER at 66.7 overall against 67.8 for unmodified reasoning on
DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B while using 78.3% of the tokens. That is the same
self-report-versus-reproduction gap this archive has been recording elsewhere,
now visible inside a single entity's definition.

**Two entities changed shape rather than gaining detail.** Omni-MATH now has a
third role: the shared-budget rationing benchmarks use it for its difficulty
labels, not its mathematics. StrategyQA is still undefined by every source
that cites it, but its role is now legible — the non-mathematical control in
an archive that is otherwise almost entirely mathematics, with ReTraceQA's
warning attached, that on commonsense QA a correct answer arrives through a
flawed trace 14–24% of the time.

**Left deliberately undone.** The definition of *Overthinking* is not merely
behind at 52 sources against 80; one clause of it is wrong. It states that
mitigation methods report "30–70% token reductions at little or no accuracy
cost", which this archive's own external-reproduction readings contradict.
It cannot be re-queued: the refresh threshold is 2.0 and this entity sits at
1.54, and lowering the threshold ranks by ratio, so it would still not surface.
The targeted route is to clear its `definition` field so render asks for it
again with all 80 sources attached. That edit was not made — it needs a
decision from the archive's owner, since clearing discards a ruling most of
which is still right.

The retry half an hour later reached arXiv cleanly and still archived nothing
